The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to create a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that:

| Requirement | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| **Operating System** | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS |
| **GPU** | NVIDIA RTX A6000 |
| **Machine type** | `n1-standard-8` (8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM – you can adjust as needed) |
| **Zone** | `us-central1-a` (or any zone that supports RTX A6000) |
| **Project ID** | `YOUR_PROJECT_ID` |
| **Instance name** | `rtx-a6000-ubuntu` |

> **NOTE**  
> *Google Cloud does **not** use “EC2”; that’s Amazon Web Services. In GCP the equivalent is a Compute Engine instance.*  
> *Make sure the Compute Engine API is enabled and that you have a service account with the `roles/compute.admin` role (or equivalent).*  

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Set your project
gcloud config set project YOUR_PROJECT_ID

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --zone us-central1-a \
  --machine-type n1-standard-8 \
  --image-family ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size 100GB \
  --boot-disk-type pd-ssd \
  --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --maintenance-policy TERMINATE \
  --restart-on-failure \
  --metadata startup-script='#!/bin/bash
    # Install NVIDIA drivers
    sudo apt-get update
    sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
    # Verify installation
    nvidia-smi
  '
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--zone` | The zone where the instance will live. RTX A6000 GPUs are available in `us-central1-a`, `us-east1-b`, etc. |
| `--machine-type` | CPU & RAM allocation. |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Pull the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` & `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk of 100 GB. |
| `--accelerator` | Attach one RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `--maintenance-policy TERMINATE` | If the host machine is reclaimed, the VM will terminate (default is MIGRATE). |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restart if the VM crashes. |
| `--metadata startup-script` | Bash script that runs on first boot to install NVIDIA drivers. |

> **Tip:** If you need a different GPU count or machine type, just change the values accordingly.

---

## 2. Using the REST API (JSON)

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine API directly (e.g., from a custom application), here’s the JSON payload you would POST to:

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535\nnvidia-smi"
      }
    ]
  },
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "TERMINATE",
    "automaticRestart": true
  }
}
```

### How to call it

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/instances"
```

Replace `YOUR_PROJECT_ID` with your actual project ID and `instance.json` with the path to the JSON file above.

---

## 3. Quick Checklist

1. **Enable APIs**  
   ```bash
   gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com
   ```

2. **Create a Service Account** (if using REST)  
   ```bash
   gcloud iam service-accounts create my-sa \
     --display-name="Compute Engine SA"
   gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding YOUR_PROJECT_ID \
     --member="serviceAccount:my-sa@YOUR_PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
     --role="roles/compute.admin"
   ```

3. **Set the default zone** (optional but handy)  
   ```bash
   gcloud config set compute/zone us-central1-a
   ```

4. **Run the `gcloud` command** or the REST call.

---

### Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix |
|---------|--------------|-----|
| `ERROR: (gcloud.compute.instances.create) Resource not found: nvidia-tesla-a6000` | Wrong accelerator type or zone | Verify the zone supports RTX A6000 (`us-central1-a`, `us-east1-b`, etc.) |
| `ERROR: (gcloud.compute.instances.create) quota exceeded` | GPU quota reached | Request a quota increase via the Cloud Console → IAM & Admin → Quotas. |
| `nvidia-smi` fails after boot | Driver not installed | Ensure the startup script runs correctly; check serial port logs. |

---

That’s all! Once the instance is running, you can SSH into it and start using the RTX A6000 GPU for your workloads. Happy computing!
